searchAudit.objective: Test whether mixed-traffic nonparticipant externalities or partner changes expose an algorithm-changing gap in cooperative autonomous driving, while refusing metric-only, transfer-only, repository-only, mock-only, fusion, uncertainty, communication-compression, and benchmark-audit ideas.
scope: socially compatible planning and mixed-traffic games
individual rationality, benefit allocation, and opt-out incentives
explicitExclusions: unmodified transfer of social navigation, SVO, ad-hoc teamwork, or zero-shot coordination to V2X
numeric candidate scoring or inferred acceptance thresholds

candidateHardStops.application: A candidate was rejected when its motivating behavior existed only as a configurable or mock-injected event without natural, field, or public-task evidence.
Porting courtesy, SVO, maximin welfare, Other-Play, FCP, COLE, BDP, few-shot adaptation, or teammate inference to V2X was treated as a collision unless the driving-specific causal object changed.
A repository link was not credited as an execution chain until a fixed commit, relevant artifacts, and runnable entry point were checked.
Unit fixtures and synthetic partner swaps were not accepted as evidence of real planner incompatibility or outsider harm.
A negative result was retained only when it would change an algorithm or deployment decision.

sourceAttempts.note: Local papers and reviews supplied prior-decision and navigation evidence, not primary scientific references. All 26 cooperative v8/v9 audit files were frozen separately.

sourceAttempts.method: arXiv abstract and linked official project verification
sourceAttempts.note: Preprints were retained only for claims visible on their primary records; formal DOI pages were preferred when available.

sourceAttempts.method: IEEE, ScienceDirect, ACM, PNAS, and institutional publication pages
sourceAttempts.note: Formal publisher or institutional destinations were used for field experiments, human studies, lane-change methods, and coalition mechanisms.

sourceAttempts.method: PMLR and official NeurIPS proceedings pages
sourceAttempts.note: Proceedings records anchor mixed-autonomy, ad-hoc teamwork, zero-shot coordination, fairness, and adaptation claims.

sourceAttempts.method: GitHub repository, commit, tree, license, tests, and entry-point inspection
sourceAttempts.note: Code checks are execution evidence only and are not counted among verified scientific references.

deduplication.policy: DOI is canonical when a formal destination exists; otherwise arXiv, PMLR, or official proceedings IDs are canonical. Repository commits are separate asset evidence.
deduplication.candidateCanonicalization: Candidates with the same intervention, causal unit, and deployment consequence were placed in one functional-equivalence cluster even when their proposed metric or terminology differed.

candidateGeneration.collisionRule: A candidate was rejected or merged when its only distinction was a new metric, a V2X application label, a partner-matrix benchmark, an unobserved mock event, or a public repository without a two-week task chain.

verifiedReferences.title: MDrive: Multi-Agent Closed-Loop Cooperative Driving with Real2Sim and Human-in-the-Loop Toolboxes
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Provides 225 cooperative-driving scenarios grounded in NHTSA typologies and real V2X datasets, and reports that negotiation can hurt planning in complex dense scenes despite aggregate multi-agent gains.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Does not isolate harm to excluded nonparticipants or report cross-play across independently trained planners.

verifiedReferences.title: Design and Evaluation of an Automated Vehicle Field Experiment: Metrics and Lessons Learned
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Documents the CIRCLES 100-vehicle open-road experiment and metrics intended to capture effects on surrounding traffic.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Establishes occurrence and measurement of traffic spillovers, not a V2X coalition-versus-outsider counterfactual.

verifiedReferences.title: Traffic Control via Connected and Automated Vehicles: An Open-Road Field Experiment with 100 Connected and Automated Vehicles
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Reports an open-road intervention using 100 connected automated vehicles and a cloud-delivered speed planner in surrounding traffic.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: The field intervention concerns traffic smoothing rather than cooperative maneuver membership or excluded-road-user harm.

verifiedReferences.title: Dissipation of Stop-and-Go Waves via Control of Autonomous Vehicles: Field Experiments
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Field experiments show that one controlled vehicle can change the motion and fuel-relevant behavior of surrounding human-driven traffic.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: The controlled action is not a V2X cooperative maneuver and the reported effect is beneficial traffic smoothing.

verifiedReferences.title: Impact of Communications Delay on Connected and Automated Vehicle Performance: An Empirical Study Using Field Data
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Uses field data to quantify how communication delay affects connected automated vehicle control performance.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Does not identify a nonparticipant cohort or partner-policy mismatch.

verifiedReferences.title: Emergent Behaviors in Mixed-Autonomy Traffic
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Shows that learned autonomous-vehicle policies can induce system-level traffic behavior in mixed-autonomy settings.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: The objective is aggregate traffic performance, not membership-conditioned externality or V2X messaging.

verifiedReferences.title: Benchmarks for Reinforcement Learning in Mixed-Autonomy Traffic
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Introduces Flow mixed-autonomy benchmark tasks and public simulation infrastructure.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: A benchmark by itself is not an idea; it is useful only as a lightweight execution substrate.

verifiedReferences.title: The Price of Anarchy for Transportation Networks with Mixed Autonomy
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Analyzes network inefficiency under mixed vehicle autonomy and bounds aggregate equilibrium cost.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Network-level equilibrium cost does not identify an episode-level excluded actor harmed by one cooperative maneuver.

verifiedReferences.title: Pricing Traffic Networks with Mixed Vehicle Autonomy
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Studies pricing mechanisms for mixed-autonomy routing externalities.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Pricing route choices is functionally different from a real-time cooperative-maneuver admission rule.

verifiedReferences.title: Routing Equilibrium in Mixed-Autonomy Traffic Networks with Altruistic Autonomous Agents
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Derives conditions under which altruistic autonomous agents improve, worsen, or leave unchanged network social cost.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: The unit is a routing equilibrium, not a message-conditioned local interaction episode.

verifiedReferences.title: When Altruism Meets Autonomy: Mixed Traffic Equilibria with Socially-Aware Autonomous Vehicles
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Studies how socially aware autonomous routing changes mixed-traffic equilibria.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Does not separate coalition members from excluded nearby road users.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Compliance Control for Socially Optimal Mixed Traffic Routing
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Develops compliance control intended to move mixed-traffic routing toward a social optimum.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: This directly occupies generic compliance and aggregate-welfare ideas but not event-level outsider non-regression.

verifiedReferences.title: Socially Compatible Control Design of Automated Vehicle in Mixed Traffic
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Optimizes an automated vehicle objective that includes its own reward and courtesy toward a following human-driven vehicle.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly collides with a generic courtesy term; it does not use a paired no-message counterfactual or excluded-cohort veto.

verifiedReferences.title: Socially Compliant Control of Connected and Automated Vehicles in Mixed Traffic for Eco-Driving
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Uses social value orientation and real highway data to model a connected automated vehicle's effect on a following human-driven vehicle.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Already occupies SVO-based neighbor utility; transferring it to a V2X coalition is not new.

verifiedReferences.title: Social Behavior for Autonomous Vehicles
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Demonstrates socially aware autonomous-driving behavior grounded in human social preferences.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: A general social preference objective does not define coalition membership or a deployment veto.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Optimal Control of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles in Mixed Traffic Using Social Value Orientation
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Formulates CAV-HDV cooperation as a potential game parameterized by social value orientation.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly blocks a generic SVO-to-V2X method transfer.

verifiedReferences.title: Pay to Change Lanes: A Cooperative Lane-Changing Strategy for Connected Vehicles
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Uses transferable utility and bargaining so a vehicle can compensate another for cooperation and refusal remains meaningful.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly occupies generic compensation, individual-rationality, and opt-out proposals.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Energy and Time-Optimal Lane Change Maneuvers with Minimal Highway Traffic Disruption
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Optimizes cooperative lane changes while explicitly minimizing disruption to highway traffic.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: It is a strong direct baseline for outsider effects; the residual gap must be membership-conditioned counterfactual admission, not another disruption cost.

verifiedReferences.title: A Self-Organizing Connected and Automated Vehicle System Based on Coalitional Game Theory
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Uses Pareto-oriented coalition formation and transferable credit for connected automated vehicles.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly occupies coalition-benefit allocation and stability; excluded nonmembers are not the causal estimand.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Driving in Heterogeneous Mixed Traffic: A Game Theoretic Approach
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Models CAV-HDV interaction with a non-cooperative leader game and inverse reinforcement learning from naturalistic human-driving data.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Heterogeneous driver modeling is not independently trained planner cross-play, and the linked repository lacks a runnable implementation at the checked commit.

verifiedReferences.title: Toward Cooperative Driving in Mixed Traffic: An Adaptive Potential Game with Field Test
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Uses adaptive potential games, Shapley-style marginal utility, human-driver preferences, and a field test for cooperative driving.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly occupies Shapley allocation and participant-specific benefit ideas; it does not test worst excluded nonparticipant counterfactual harm.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Merging in Mixed Traffic of Connected and Automated Vehicles and Human-Driven Vehicles
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Provides a direct cooperative merging method for mixed connected-automated and human-driven traffic.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: A maneuver method is a baseline, not evidence of partner-generalization novelty.

verifiedReferences.title: Intent-Aware Planning in Heterogeneous Traffic via Distributed Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Develops distributed intent-aware planning for heterogeneous traffic participants.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Heterogeneous traffic intent does not supply independently trained cooperative planner partners or an outsider-veto causal contrast.

verifiedReferences.title: UniV2X: End-to-End Autonomous Driving through Vehicle-to-Everything Cooperation
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Provides an end-to-end V2X cooperative perception-and-planning system.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Its cooperative gain is participant-side; the source does not identify excluded actors or planner cross-play. Perception fusion aspects are out of scope.

verifiedReferences.title: Toward Collaborative Autonomous Driving: Simulation Platform and End-to-End System
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Introduces V2Xverse and an end-to-end collaborative driving system with cooperative planning evaluation.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: The public stack is CARLA-heavy and does not provide matched independently trained planners for lightweight cross-play.

verifiedReferences.title: Other-Play for Zero-Shot Coordination
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Addresses zero-shot coordination by making policies robust to symmetry-equivalent conventions.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Applying Other-Play unchanged to driving is method transfer, not a new driving causal problem.

verifiedReferences.title: Collaborating with Humans without Human Data
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Introduces fictitious co-play using a population of synthetic partners to improve coordination with unseen humans.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: A driving deployment would need a distinct mechanism and public partner suite; a direct port is rejected.

verifiedReferences.title: COLE: Cooperative Open-Ended Learning Framework for Zero-Shot Coordination
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Uses open-ended partner generation and learning to improve zero-shot coordination.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly occupies generic partner-population and co-evolution proposals.

verifiedReferences.title: Behavior Diversity Play for Zero-Shot Coordination
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Trains against behaviorally diverse partners for zero-shot coordination.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly occupies generic diversity-conditioned partner training.

verifiedReferences.title: ZSC-Eval: An Evaluation Toolkit and Benchmark for Multi-agent Zero-Shot Coordination
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Provides a standardized zero-shot coordination evaluation toolkit, policy pools, and cross-play result artifacts.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: A partner-swap matrix alone remains a benchmark audit and its environments are not cooperative driving.

verifiedReferences.title: Cross-Environment Cooperation Enables Zero-Shot Multi-Agent Coordination
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Uses cross-environment cooperative training to improve zero-shot coordination.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Porting the training recipe to driving is not sufficient novelty.

verifiedReferences.title: Towards Few-Shot Coordination: Revisiting Ad-hoc Teamplay Challenge in the Game of Hanabi
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Evaluates adaptation among independently trained agents and measures few-shot coordination across methods.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly occupies generic few-shot partner adaptation; the public task is not driving.

verifiedReferences.title: Graph-based Policy Adaptation for Ad Hoc Teamwork
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Uses graph-conditioned policy adaptation for ad-hoc teamwork with changing teammates.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: A planner-type adapter in V2X would be a direct method transfer without a distinct driving estimand.

verifiedReferences.title: HOLA: Human-in-the-Loop Open Adaptive Multi-Robot Teaming
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Studies open adaptive teaming under changing human and robot partners.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Its adaptation framing is a direct prior, while the task and safety consequences differ from road traffic.

verifiedReferences.title: Learning to Negotiate via Voluntary Commitment
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Introduces voluntary commitment as a learned negotiation mechanism in multi-agent interaction.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly blocks a generic opt-out or voluntary-message proposal without driving-specific occurrence evidence.

verifiedReferences.title: Learning Fair Policies in Decentralized Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Optimizes decentralized cooperative policies under alternative social welfare and fairness objectives.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly occupies generic maximin, welfare, and fairness reward substitutions; metrics alone do not change V2X deployment.

verifiedReferences.title: Robust Autonomy Emerges from Self-Play
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Shows that self-play can produce robustness to varied interaction partners in a cooperative setting.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Self-play robustness is a generic partner-generalization method, not a driving-specific causal claim.

verifiedReferences.title: Dreaming to Assist: Learning to Coordinate with Unknown Agents from Imagined Trajectories
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Learns to assist unknown partners using imagined partner trajectories.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly occupies generic online partner-model and assistance proposals.

verifiedReferences.title: Understanding Human-Machine Cooperation in Mixed Traffic Through a Human-Centered Study
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Provides primary human-centered evidence about human-machine cooperation in mixed traffic.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Does not expose a public message-labeled trajectory cohort suitable for causal V2X-message externality estimation.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Formation of Autonomous Vehicles in Mixed Traffic Beyond Platooning
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Optimizes cooperative formation behavior for automated vehicles embedded in mixed traffic.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: The formation objective does not define nonmember non-regression or unseen planner partners.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Lane Change Considering the Effect of Following Vehicles on Both Lanes
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Explicitly incorporates effects on following vehicles in both source and target lanes during cooperative lane change.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Directly blocks a generic following-vehicle cost term; it is a required baseline for any residual outsider claim.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative Lane-Changing Strategy in Mixed Traffic Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Develops a deep-reinforcement-learning cooperative lane-changing strategy for mixed traffic.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: It contributes a maneuver baseline but not excluded-cohort counterfactual identification.

verifiedReferences.title: Connected and Automated Vehicle Lane Changes in Mixed Traffic: Modeling and Impact Analysis
verifiedReferences.verifiedClaim: Analyzes how connected automated vehicle lane changes affect mixed-traffic behavior, including adverse traffic impacts under some conditions.
verifiedReferences.limitationForThisAudit: Does not isolate V2X cooperation as treatment or define coalition outsiders.

candidateLedger.title: Counterfactual Nonparticipant Non-Regression for Cooperative Maneuver Admission
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Before executing a V2X cooperative maneuver, evaluate the same downstream planner twice on the same state: once with the cooperative message set and once with those peer messages masked. Reject or reorder the cooperative branch when its predicted worst excluded-actor braking or wait burden exceeds the fallback branch; otherwise allow it.
candidateLedger.algorithmOrDeploymentChange: Adds a lexicographic nonparticipant non-regression admission layer to the cooperative planner. The output changes which cooperative plan can execute, rather than adding a reporting metric.
candidateLedger.naturalOrPublicEvidence: MDrive publicly exposes negotiation routes and reports planning degradation in complex dense scenes. CIRCLES, the 100-CAV field experiment, and stop-and-go field experiments establish that automated interventions can change surrounding traffic. Mixed-traffic lane-change studies explicitly show following-vehicle effects. These sources establish an occurrence mechanism and public test cohorts, but none proves the proposed membership-conditioned sign reversal.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: Socially compatible, SVO, minimal-disruption, coalition, and Shapley methods internalize neighbor or participant utility directly. No verified source in this audit performed a per-event cooperative-message versus masked-message contrast, defined the harmed cohort by exclusion from the cooperation set, and used that contrast as a hard maneuver-admission rule.
candidateLedger.v2xIrreplaceableDifference: Coalition membership and the message-masked paired plan define the treatment. Without V2X participation metadata and the cooperative message branch, the excluded cohort and intervention are not identifiable.

candidateLedger.title: Coalition-Only Success Versus Outsider Harm Sign-Reversal Audit
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Report whether participant success improves while a nonparticipant braking or wait metric worsens.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: This is the measurement-only half of coalition-outsider-counterfactual-veto and does not change the planner or deployment decision.

candidateLedger.title: Externality-Budgeted V2X Coalition Formation
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Add an outsider-cost budget to coalition formation and admit coalitions under that budget.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: Without the paired message counterfactual, this is a renamed traffic-disruption, SVO, or social-welfare constraint; the budget also introduces an unsupported acceptance threshold.

candidateLedger.title: Voluntary Exit from a Cooperative Maneuver
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Allow a participant to withdraw when its predicted utility is lower than acting alone.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: Pay-to-change-lanes, voluntary commitment, adaptive potential games, and coalitional-game work directly occupy refusal, compensation, participant preferences, and individual rationality.

candidateLedger.title: Shapley Redistribution of Cooperative Driving Benefit
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Redistribute cooperative benefit according to each participant's marginal contribution.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: Adaptive-potential-game field work already uses Shapley-style marginal utility, while coalitional-game driving and transferable-utility lane change already allocate or compensate participant benefit.

candidateLedger.title: Worst-Member Risk-Sensitive Cooperative Reward
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Replace team-average success with a worst-participant, maximin, or inequality-sensitive objective.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: This is a generic cooperative-MARL welfare substitution and does not require V2X or identify a driving-specific intervention.

candidateLedger.title: Human Braking Effect of Cooperative Messages
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Estimate whether cooperative messages cause nearby human drivers to brake or wait more.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: The local control-game pool already rejected message-action attribution in MDrive. Available human and field data do not jointly expose message, planner branch, and matched human response; a new analysis would therefore be audit-only or mock-injected.

candidateLedger.title: Cross-Play Matrix for Unseen Cooperative Driving Planners
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Swap independently trained planners and report pairwise success degradation.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: This is a pure benchmark audit, collides with the prior minimal-cross-play-semantics reject, and lacks a public matched driving planner pool.

candidateLedger.title: Fictitious Co-Play Population for V2X Planners
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Train a cooperative driving policy against a diverse synthetic population of teammate planners.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: FCP, COLE, behavior-diversity play, cross-environment cooperation, and self-play robustness directly occupy the method; changing the environment to V2X is not novelty.

candidateLedger.title: Online Inference and Adaptation to an Unknown Partner Planner
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Infer a teammate planner type from a short interaction history and adapt the ego policy online.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: Few-shot coordination, graph policy adaptation, open adaptive teaming, and imagined-trajectory assistance directly occupy this method family; no public driving partner suite supports a distinct two-week test.

candidateLedger.title: Fallback Selection under Cooperative Planner Shift
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Detect an unfamiliar partner and select a conservative fallback planner.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: Collides with the prior cross-planner commitment-acceptance and planner-agnostic contract rejects, while generic unknown-partner adaptation already supplies the method.

candidateLedger.title: Outsider-Harm Shield under Partner Swap
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Apply an outsider-harm shield specifically when a cooperative planner is paired with an unseen partner.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: Combines the retained outsider-veto mechanism with a generic partner-shift condition but cannot separate the two contributions without matched independently trained planners and natural cross-play failures.

candidateLedger.title: Human Opt-Out from a V2X Yield Request
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Expose an opt-out or refusal response for a human-driven vehicle asked to yield to a V2X coalition.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: Voluntary commitment, pay-to-change-lanes, bargaining, and compliance control directly occupy refusal and compensation, while no natural message-response cohort exposes this intervention.

candidateLedger.title: Pedestrian Right-of-Way Debt from Cooperative Maneuvers
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Accumulate a debt when cooperative vehicles make a pedestrian wait and optimize repayment in later actions.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: The debt is a generic fairness or social-navigation metric, and no public evidence links a cooperative message branch to matched pedestrian response or later repayment behavior.

candidateLedger.title: Reanalysis of Field Spillovers around Controlled Vehicles
candidateLedger.coreIntervention: Reanalyze CIRCLES or related field trajectories for worst-neighbor braking and delay.
candidateLedger.functionalCollisionFinding: This can strengthen evidence for occurrence but does not isolate V2X cooperation or change a planning algorithm. It is evidence work, not a retained idea.

shortlist.title: Counterfactual Nonparticipant Non-Regression for Cooperative Maneuver Admission
shortlist.whyItSurvives: It changes the deployable action by requiring a same-state, same-planner cooperative-message versus masked-message comparison for actors excluded from the cooperation set. The causal object is not supplied by generic fairness, SVO, coalition allocation, or zero-shot partner methods, and a public lightweight scenario path was actually loaded.

causalDefinitions.coalition: The V2X senders and receivers whose messages are consumed to produce the candidate cooperative maneuver in episode e.
causalDefinitions.nonparticipantSet: Tracked road users in the interaction envelope who are not coalition members and do not choose the coalition action. The set is frozen before comparing the two planner branches.
causalDefinitions.cooperativeBranch: The downstream planner output using the observed cooperative message set.
causalDefinitions.fallbackBranch: The same downstream planner, state, prediction horizon, and random seed with peer cooperative messages masked and the documented ego-only fallback enabled.
causalDefinitions.admissionRule: Execute the cooperative branch only when its predicted worst nonparticipant burden does not exceed the fallback branch. Otherwise execute or replan from the fallback branch. This is lexicographic non-regression and introduces no tuned acceptance threshold.

estimands.primaryOutsiderBrakingContrast: Delta_brake = E_e[max_{j in N_e} integral_0^T max(0,-a_j^coop(t)) dt - max_{j in N_e} integral_0^T max(0,-a_j^fallback(t)) dt]
estimands.algorithmEffect: Delta_veto = E_e[H_out(e, vetoed_admission) - H_out(e, unshielded_cooperation)], where H_out is fixed before evaluation as worst-actor braking impulse with conflict-zone wait as a separate secondary endpoint.
estimands.identificationNote: Primary evidence is paired within the same physical episode seed and actor initialization. Actors, frames, and repeated horizons are not treated as independent replicates.

independentUnit.unit: One physical conflict episode defined by route template, initial actor state, human-driver response realization, and random seed, paired across planner branches.
notIndependent: multiple actors from the same episode
independentUnit.analysis: Episode-level paired contrasts with route-template blocking and an episode-level paired bootstrap; report the distribution and sign stability rather than frame-level significance.

strongBaselines: same planner with cooperative messages masked and ego-only fallback
socially compatible or SVO courtesy controller from arxiv:2112.02041 and arxiv:2203.17106
minimal-traffic-disruption cooperative lane change from doi:10.1016/j.automatica.2024.111651
adaptive-potential-game or Shapley participant-utility controller from arxiv:2604.20231

naturalOrPublicDataEvidence.evidence: MDrive's public scenario taxonomy includes lane-change negotiation routes, and the paper reports that negotiation can degrade planning in dense complex scenes.
naturalOrPublicDataEvidence.boundary: This motivates the event family but does not establish outsider-specific harm.

naturalOrPublicDataEvidence.evidence: CIRCLES and related 100-CAV and stop-and-go field experiments show that automated interventions measurably change surrounding traffic.
naturalOrPublicDataEvidence.boundary: These observations establish spillover occurrence, not the sign of a V2X membership-conditioned effect.

naturalOrPublicDataEvidence.evidence: Mixed-traffic cooperative lane-change papers model following-vehicle disruption and adverse lane-change effects.
naturalOrPublicDataEvidence.boundary: They are required direct baselines and prevent claiming that neighbor costs are themselves new.

twoWeekGoNoGo.days1To3: Use the pinned MDrive loader to enumerate all 15 public route leaves and freeze the five lane-change-negotiation variants. Set up the pinned Flow merge or ring path if its old dependency stack remains installable; otherwise use MDrive route metadata plus an already public lightweight kinematic response layer, with no mock occurrence claim.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days4To8: Implement the paired cooperative-message and masked-message planner call with a frozen nonparticipant set and lexicographic veto. Use at least two documented human-driver response models or independent public parameter cohorts.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days9To12: Run episode-paired comparisons against all six baselines. Reopen traces where participant gain and outsider burden have opposite signs; reject any effect caused only by actor-set changes or horizon leakage.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days13To14: Complete collision review against SVO, minimal-disruption, coalition, and Shapley baselines and decide go or no-go from the preregistered conditions.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: At least one public or naturally grounded scenario family exhibits repeatable participant gain together with positive excluded-actor burden under unshielded cooperation, and the veto reduces that burden while preserving nonzero participant gain in some episodes, with the effect not reproduced by SVO, all-actor welfare, minimal-disruption, or Shapley baselines.
noGoConditions: No stable participant-gain versus outsider-burden sign reversal appears at the episode level.
The effect appears only under an injected or undocumented human-response model.
An existing socially compatible, minimal-disruption, or adaptive-potential-game baseline dominates the veto on the same causal contrast.
The public chain cannot connect coalition messages, both planner branches, and nonparticipant response without full-stack reconstruction.
The nonparticipant set changes between branches or requires post-treatment membership definitions.

shortlist.positiveResultValue: Would justify a deployable cooperative-maneuver admission layer and require participant-only V2X evaluations to expose an excluded-road-user causal contrast before deployment.
shortlist.negativeResultValue: Would rule out the proposed veto in the tested operational domain and support using the simpler socially compatible, minimal-disruption, or participant-utility planner without a new membership-conditioned guard.
publicExecutionChain: MDrive official repository at 9e08377042b8f2e2860bb00de2416b3ebcfa3be4: route discovery and 14 scenario-discovery tests passed without CARLA; 15 route leaves and 5 negotiation variants were loaded.

Flow official repository at a511c41c48e6b928bb2060de8ad1ef3c3e3d9554: fixed tree exposes public mixed-autonomy merge, ring, highway, multi-agent configurations, controllers, and trained-ring results; local setup is an explicit first-week gate because clone timed out and the commit is old.
All causal contrasts can be produced in a lightweight mixed-autonomy simulator before any optional full MDrive CARLA run. Full CARLA is not required for the go/no-go decision.
knownRisks: Flow's fixed public stack is old and may require environment repair, so failure of its setup is a no-go rather than evidence for novelty.
MDrive route discovery is public and runnable, but full planner trajectories still require CARLA and checkpoints.
A response-model-only sign reversal is insufficient; at least one public or naturally grounded parameter cohort must support it.
The veto may collapse to existing minimal-disruption control after direct baseline comparison.

conclusion.summary: One narrow residual survived: use V2X coalition membership and a same-planner message-masked counterfactual to veto cooperative maneuvers that worsen the worst excluded road user's braking or waiting burden. Existing evidence shows that automated actions affect surrounding traffic and that dense negotiation can degrade planning, but it does not yet prove the retained sign reversal; that is the two-week gate. All standalone partner-generalization ideas were rejected because they collide with ad-hoc or zero-shot coordination methods, prior local cross-play rejects, and the absence of a matched lightweight public driving partner suite.

conclusion.executionEvidence: At MDrive commit 9e08377042b8f2e2860bb00de2416b3ebcfa3be4, 14 scenario-discovery tests passed and the real public route loader enumerated 15 scenarios, including 5 negotiation variants, without CARLA. ZSC-Eval was pinned and inspected but its parser stopped at a missing absl dependency; no extra dependency installation was pursued. Flow and NCLGame-IRL were checked at fixed commits with their execution limits recorded.
